method: Same indicator definitions, traffic-light thresholds and layer weights as the regular report (monitor.py), applied to every Friday. Six indicators whose level means something different in the past are left out, and so is the credit layer (ICE BofA spreads, BIZD), because the public source only offers about three years of spread history; an indicator or layer with no data at a date is skipped and its weight shared among the rest. Not the same number as the 20-indicator score of the regular report, and blind to credit spreads: compare history with `latest`. `recent` is the other ruler: the full 20-indicator rule of the regular report on every business day of the roughly three years for which real credit spreads exist. Over those years the two scores barely move together (correlation 0.06 in the 2026-11-25 check), so they are two separate gauges and are never joined into one line.
sources: FRED (Cboe VIX, Chicago Fed NFCI, St. Louis Fed STLFSI4, Sahm, CP, T-bill, 2s10s), Yahoo Finance (MOVE), Bank of Korea ECOS
